Understanding Market Microstructure

Market making strategies rely on understanding order flow toxicity (Easley et al., 2012). The VPIN metric introduced in that work [1] has become a standard tool for high-frequency trading firms (Menkveld, 2013)(Biais et al., 2015).

The VPIN toxicity metric formula [Easley et al., 2012]

Recent empirical studies [2][3] have validated the VPIN approach. However, Andersen and Bondarenko (2019) raised concerns about its robustness during periods of extreme volatility [4].

The bid-ask spread can be decomposed into three components: adverse selection, inventory, and order processing costs (Huang and Stoll, 1997). Understanding these components is essential for designing effective market making algorithms (Avellaneda and Stoikov, 2008)(Guilbaud and Pham, 2013).

References

  1. Easley, D., López de Prado, M.M. and O'Hara, M. (2012). Flow toxicity and liquidity in a high frequency world. Review of Financial Studies.
  2. Hagströmer, B. and Nordén, L. (2013). The diversity of high-frequency traders. Journal of Financial Markets.
